Definition: from G3498; to deaden, i.e. (figuratively) to subdue:--be dead, mortify.
BiblicalUsage: Paul tells the Colossians to mortify their members upon the earth, and Abraham's body is described as good as dead when the promise of a son is given. The same word names the deadness of Abraham's body and the mortifying of the Christian's members.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe mortifying is putting to death what is already dead: Abraham's body could not give life, and my members cannot give life either, and the life comes only from the God who raises the dead. The members I mortify are the ones He has already judged, and the life I live is the one He gives.
